title_en: Notice of the General Office of the Supreme People's Court on Forwarding the Guiding Opinions of the Supreme People's Procuratorate on the Application of the Regulations on Several Issues Concerning the Review and Judgment of Evidence in Death Penalty Cases and the Regulations on Several Issues Concerning the Exclusion of Illegal Evidence in Criminal Cases
keywords_en: handling death penalty cases; handling criminal cases
full_text_en:
Office of the Supreme People's Court

Notice on Forwarding the Supreme People's Procuratorate's "Guiding Opinions on the Application of the 'Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Examination and Judgment of Evidence in Death Penalty Cases' and the 'Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Exclusion of Illegally Obtained Evidence in Criminal Cases'"

Fa Ban [2011] No. 47

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Supreme People's Procuratorate's "Guiding Opinions on the Application of the 'Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Examination and Judgment of Evidence in Death Penalty Cases' and the 'Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Exclusion of Illegally Obtained Evidence in Criminal Cases'" (hereinafter referred to as the "Guiding Opinions") was issued on December 30, 2010. The Guiding Opinions strengthen legal supervision over investigation and evidence collection, strengthen the burden of proof regarding the legality of evidence, and strengthen the comprehensive review and use of evidence. It may serve as a basis for people's courts and people's procuratorates to jointly implement the two Evidence Provisions and to review and evaluate evidence. It is hereby forwarded to you for reference in your trial work. Please effectively implement the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Examination and Judgment of Evidence in Death Penalty Cases" and the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Exclusion of Illegally Obtained Evidence in Criminal Cases" in accordance with the Guiding Opinions, ensure the quality of criminal case trials, and strive for better adjudicative results.

March 3, 2011

Guiding Opinions on the Application of the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Examination and Judgment of Evidence in Death Penalty Cases" and the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Exclusion of Illegally Obtained Evidence in Criminal Cases"

With a view to correctly applying the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Examination and Judgment of Evidence in Death Penalty Cases" and the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Exclusion of Illegally Obtained Evidence in Criminal Cases" (hereinafter referred to as the two "Provisions") jointly issued by the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security, and the Ministry of Justice, the following Guiding Opinions are put forward in light of the actual circumstances of procuratorial organs in handling cases.

I. Earnestly Implement the Two Provisions and Improve the Level of Law Enforcement and Case Handling

1. The two Provisions are of great significance for further improving China's criminal procedure system, regulating law enforcement and case handling conduct, improving the level of law enforcement and case handling, protecting human rights according to law, and advancing the construction of socialist rule of law. Procuratorial organs at all levels must study deeply, accurately understand, and grasp the two Provisions, unify their thinking, raise their awareness, insist on emphasizing facts, evidence, law, and responsibility, firmly establish the concept of balancing the fight against crime with the protection of human rights, and balancing substantive justice with procedural justice, and take the implementation of the two Provisions as an opportunity to comprehensively improve the level of law enforcement and case handling.

2. Vigorously strengthen the awareness of evidence, and strictly collect, fix, review, judge, and use evidence in accordance with the two Provisions. Focus on the comprehensive review and use of evidence, carefully reviewing not only the objectivity and relevance of evidence but also its legality. Strictly control the aspects of facts, evidence, procedures, and law, ensuring that there are no contradictions between evidence and evidence, or between evidence and the facts of the case, or that contradictions are reasonably eliminated, so that cases with unclear facts are not finalized, and cases with insufficient evidence are not prosecuted, effectively preventing wrongful and unjust cases.

3. The two Provisions set higher standards and stricter requirements for handling death penalty cases. Procuratorial organs at all levels must comprehensively strengthen the handling and supervision of death penalty cases, earnestly fulfill the duties conferred by law, conduct stricter reviews of evidence, adhere to stricter standards of proof, and ensure the quality of handling death penalty cases.

4. Procuratorial organs at all levels must earnestly fulfill their supervisory functions, strengthen supervision over the collection and fixation of evidence, and strengthen supervision over the admission and exclusion of evidence. Insist on organically combining the supervision and correction of individual cases with the correction of universal problems, routine supervision with special supervision, and strengthening supervision with coordination and cooperation, and equally emphasize strengthening legal supervision and strengthening self-supervision, so as to dare to supervise, be good at supervising, supervise according to law, and supervise in a standardized manner, ensuring that criminal proceedings are conducted strictly in accordance with the law.

II. Further Standardize the Case Handling Procedures for Duty Crime Cases and Collect Evidence Objectively According to Law

5. When handling duty crime cases, the People's Procuratorate shall collect and fix evidence strictly according to law. It shall not only collect various evidence proving the facts of the case but also promptly fix evidence proving the legality of the evidence collection process, ensuring that the facts of the case are clear, the evidence is reliable and sufficient, and the evidence collection procedures are lawful.

6. When handling duty crime cases, the People's Procuratorate shall collect and fix evidence comprehensively and objectively. It shall not only collect various evidence proving the criminal suspect's guilt and serious crime but also collect various evidence proving the criminal suspect's innocence and minor crime.

7. Strictly implement the system of simultaneous audio and video recording of the entire process of interrogating criminal suspects in duty crime cases. If the relevant provisions are not strictly implemented, or if falsification in implementation causes adverse consequences, the primary responsible persons shall be held accountable in accordance with the relevant provisions.

8. The departments of investigation supervision, public prosecution, and complaints and appeals shall, in accordance with the requirements of the two Provisions, strengthen the review and supervision of the activities of collecting and fixing evidence by the investigatory departments of the procuratorate, and promptly issue corrective opinions if violations of the relevant provisions are found.

III. Strictly Review and Judge Evidence to Ensure Case Handling Quality

9. Strictly abide by the rules established by the two Provisions, carefully review, identify, and analyze evidence, and correctly determine the facts of the case. It is necessary to review not only whether the content of the evidence is true and objective and whether the form is lawful and complete but also whether the process of evidence collection is lawful; it is necessary not only to exclude illegal evidence according to law but also to do a good job of reviewing, correcting, and perfecting defective evidence.

10. With respect to the confessions of criminal suspects and the testimony of witnesses and statements of victims, their objective authenticity shall be comprehensively reviewed in conjunction with other evidence in the whole case, and at the same time, it shall be reviewed whether the investigative organ (department) has transferred all records of each interrogation and inquiry. Confessions of criminal suspects obtained by illegal means such as extortion of confessions by torture, and testimony of witnesses and statements of victims obtained by illegal means such as violence or threats, shall be excluded according to law; for confessions of criminal suspects, testimony of witnesses, and statements of victims obtained by other illegal means, a decision on whether to exclude them according to law shall be made based on the degree of harm of the illegality and whether it is comparable to extortion of confessions by torture and violence or threats.

11. During the first interrogation of a criminal suspect in the process of reviewing arrest and reviewing prosecution, the suspect shall be asked whether his or her confession is true, and this shall be recorded in the record. For a criminal suspect in custody, the time of interrogation and the correspondence between the interrogator and the interrogation record shall be verified based on the records in the arrest warrant; if the interrogation took place at a place outside the detention center, the investigative organ (department) shall be required to provide an explanation of necessity, and the validity of its reasons shall be reviewed. It shall be reviewed whether the criminal suspect is proficient in the commonly used local language.

12. The confessions and defenses of a criminal suspect shall be reviewed in conjunction with all of his or her confessions and defenses and other evidence. If a criminal suspect's confession of guilt is not corroborated by other evidence, it cannot be used as a basis for approving or deciding on arrest or initiating a public prosecution; if it is corroborated by other evidence and the reasons for the innocence defense cannot be established, that confession may be used as a basis for approving or deciding on arrest or initiating a public prosecution.

13. If a criminal suspect or his or her retained lawyer claims that the suspect was subjected to extortion of confessions by torture, he or she shall be informed to truthfully provide relevant evidence or leads, and the claim shall be carefully investigated. If there is suspicion of extortion of confessions by torture, the investigative organ (department) shall be requested to provide all interrogation records, the original audio and video recordings of the interrogation process, records of health checks upon entering and leaving the detention center, records of conversations with detention center supervisory personnel, and explanations of the legality of the interrogation process; if necessary, the interrogators, other persons present, detention center supervisory personnel, or witnesses may be questioned, and relevant materials from the procuratorate's office in the detention center may be obtained. If injuries are found on the criminal suspect, a necessary investigation and appraisal of the cause and extent of the injuries shall be conducted promptly. If there are doubts about the simultaneous audio and video recordings, the investigative organ (department) may be requested to explain the reasons for any discontinuities; if necessary, the procuratorial technical department may be coordinated to conduct a review.

14. Strengthen supervision over the interrogation of criminal suspects during investigative activities. If a criminal suspect is not sent to the detention center on the same day as the decision to detain is made, it shall be ascertained where the suspect is held outside the detention center and the circumstances of the interrogation; the detention center shall be supervised to truthfully, in detail, and accurately fill in the physical examination record of the criminal suspect upon admission; if necessary, it is recommended to record the physical condition of the criminal suspect by video or photography; if it is found that the investigative organ (department) conducted interrogations outside the detention center, the time, place, reasons, approval procedures, and circumstances of the criminal suspect's interrogation outside the detention center shall be promptly understood, and procuratorial supervision over the physical examination records during the transfer and return of the suspect shall be carried out. If violations of relevant supervision regulations are found, corrective opinions or procuratorial suggestions shall be promptly issued in accordance with relevant laws and regulations, and recorded.

15. When reviewing witness testimony and victim statements, attention shall be paid to reviewing the interrogation procedures, methods, content, and form of interrogation records. If violations of regulations are found, the investigative organ (department) shall be required to make corrections or provide explanations. Attention shall be paid to reviewing whether witnesses and victims can distinguish right from wrong and express themselves correctly; if necessary, they shall be questioned and understood; at the same time, it shall be reviewed whether witnesses and victims testified individually; if witnesses or victims were questioned at a place other than that prescribed by law, the reasons shall be reviewed; if necessary, that testimony or statement shall be re-examined. Whether the content of witness testimony and victim statements is true shall be comprehensively judged in conjunction with other evidence. If a criminal suspect and his or her defender, or a witness or victim, claims that the investigative organ (department) used illegal means such as violence or threats to obtain evidence, he or she shall be informed to truthfully provide relevant evidence or leads, and the claim shall be carefully investigated.

16. With respect to physical evidence, documentary evidence, inspection and examination records, search records, audio-visual materials, and electronic evidence, it is necessary not only to review whether they objectively and truly reflect the facts of the case but also to strengthen the review of the procedures for collecting and producing the evidence and the form of the evidence. If it is found that the source, collection, and production process of physical evidence, documentary evidence, audio-visual materials, and electronic evidence are unclear, or that the form of inspection and examination records or search records does not comply with regulations or the recorded content is contradictory, the investigative organ (department) shall be required to make corrections; if corrections cannot be made, an explanation or reasonable interpretation shall be provided; if no reasonable explanation or interpretation can be provided, such evidence cannot be used as evidence; if it is found that during the inspection, examination, or search, the investigative organ (department) should have extracted but did not extract relevant traces or items that may be related to the facts of the case, the investigative organ (department) shall be required to supplement collection or retrieval; if photographs, videos, or reproductions of physical evidence do not reflect the shape and characteristics of the original object, or if copies or reproductions of documentary evidence do not reflect the characteristics and content of the original document, the investigative organ (department) shall be required to re-produce them; if it is found that physical evidence, documentary evidence, audio-visual materials, electronic evidence, etc., in the case file that should have been appraised were not appraised, the investigative organ (department) shall be required to conduct an appraisal; if necessary, a separate appraisal may be entrusted on its own.

17. The corrections, explanations, and re-collection or re-production by the investigative organ (department) shall be carefully reviewed; if necessary, a re-examination may be conducted. If the evidence is lawfully re-collected, promptly corrected, or can be reasonably interpreted by the investigative organ (department) according to law, and the authenticity of the physical or documentary evidence is not affected, it may be used as a basis for approving or deciding on arrest or initiating a public prosecution. If the investigative organ (department) fails to lawfully re-collect, correct, or cannot correct, re-produce, and fails to provide a reasonable explanation or interpretation, and the authenticity of the evidence cannot be determined, that evidence cannot be used as a basis for approving or deciding on arrest or initiating a public prosecution.

18. For physical evidence or documentary evidence of a highly concealed nature that is obtained based on the confession or identification of a criminal suspect, it is necessary to review not only whether it is corroborated by other evidence proving the commission of the crime but also whether the investigative organ (department) had knowledge of that evidence before the criminal suspect's confession or identification, and to comprehensively judge based on all the evidence in the case whether it can be used as a basis for approving or deciding on arrest or initiating a public prosecution.

19. When reviewing expert opinions, focus shall be placed on reviewing whether the source, extraction, storage, and submission for examination of the sample comply with legal and relevant regulations, whether the expert institution or expert has the legal qualifications and conditions for appraisal, whether the formal requirements of the expert opinion are complete, whether the appraisal procedure is lawful, and whether the expert conclusion is scientific and reasonable. If the source of the sample is unknown or the sample may be contaminated, causing doubts about the expert opinion, the investigative organ (department) shall be required to conduct a new appraisal or supplementary appraisal; if necessary, the procuratorial organ may separately entrust a new appraisal or supplementary appraisal; if the expert institution or expert does not have the legal qualifications and conditions for appraisal, or the subject of appraisal exceeds its scope of appraisal, or the recusal provisions are violated, the investigative organ (department) shall be required to separately entrust a new appraisal; if necessary, the procuratorial organ may separately entrust a new appraisal; if the formal requirements of the expert opinion are incomplete, the expert institution shall be required through the investigative organ (department) to make corrections; for issues involving specialized technical matters such as the appraisal procedure, method, or conclusion, the opinion of the procuratorial technical department or other persons with specialized knowledge shall be sought when necessary.

20. If it is found that investigators used illegal means such as extortion of confessions by torture or violence or threats to collect confessions of criminal suspects, statements of victims, or testimony of witnesses, corrective opinions shall be issued, and at the same time, the investigative organ (department) shall be required to assign other investigators to re-collect evidence; if necessary, the procuratorial organ may also collect evidence on its own. If the investigative organ (department) fails to assign other investigators to re-collect evidence, the case may be returned for supplementary investigation according to law. If, upon review, it is found that there were illegal evidence collection acts such as extortion of confessions by torture or violent evidence collection, and after those illegal oral evidence is excluded, other evidence cannot prove that the criminal suspect committed the criminal act, arrest shall not be approved or decided; if the case has already been transferred for review and prosecution, the case may be returned to the investigative organ (department) or a decision not to prosecute may be made. Case handlers excluding illegal evidence shall indicate this in the review report.

IV. Do a Good Job in Proving the Legality of Evidence and Enhance the Capacity to Lawfully Allege Crimes

21. Proving the legality of evidence is an important task for the procuratorial organ in lawfully alleging crimes, strengthening litigation supervision, and ensuring the quality of case handling. Adhere to strict review of the legality of evidence, lawfully exclude illegal evidence, further improve the level of court appearance for public prosecution, and do a good job in proving the legality of evidence.

22. After receiving written opinions submitted by the people's court reflecting that the defendant's pre-trial confession was illegally obtained, or relevant materials such as copies of the record of the complaint, the procuratorial organ shall promptly review them based on the relevant evidence or leads provided. If the issue was raised during the review of arrest and review of prosecution and it was verified that no illegal evidence collection act existed, preparations for trial shall be made based on the verified situation. If new evidence or leads are raised after the initiation of public prosecution, the investigative organ (department) shall be required to provide relevant proof; if necessary, the procuratorial organ may conduct its own investigation and verification.

23. During trial, if the defendant or his or her defender claims that the defendant's pre-trial confession was illegally obtained without providing relevant evidence or leads, the public prosecutor shall comprehensively explain the legality of that evidence based on the overall evidence in the case. If the defendant or his or her defender provides relevant evidence or leads, and the court, upon review, has doubts about the legality of obtaining the defendant's pre-trial confession, the public prosecutor shall provide to the court the interrogation records, records of health checks upon entering and leaving the detention center, records of conversations with detention center supervisory personnel, and explanations from the investigative organ (department) on the legality of the interrogation process; if audio and video recordings of the interrogation process exist, they shall be provided. If necessary, the court shall be requested to notify other persons present at the interrogation or other witnesses to testify in court; if the legality still cannot be proven, the court shall be requested to notify the interrogators to testify in court. For new evidence or leads raised by the defendant or his or her defender during trial that cannot be proven in court, the court shall be requested according to law to adjourn the trial, and the investigative organ (department) shall be required to provide relevant proof; if necessary, the procuratorial organ may conduct its own investigation and verification.

24. If, after comprehensive presentation and cross-examination of evidence during trial, it is believed that the legality of obtaining the defendant's pre-trial confession has already been proven, but the court still has doubts, the court may be requested to adjourn for investigation and verification of the relevant evidence. If the court conducts an out-of-court investigation and notifies the procuratorial personnel to be present, the procuratorial personnel shall be present when necessary. If there is any objection to the evidence verified by the court, the court shall be requested to re-open the trial for investigation.

25. If during trial the defendant or his or her defender claims that the written testimony of a witness not present in court or the written statement of a victim not present in court was illegally obtained, explanations on the legality may be made from aspects such as the witness's or victim's qualification to testify, the interrogator, the interrogation procedure and method, and the statutory form of the interrogation record; if original audio and video recordings of the interrogation process or other evidence can prove legality, they may be read out or presented in court. If the defendant or his or her defender raises clear new evidence or leads requiring further investigation and verification, the court shall be requested according to law to adjourn the trial, and the investigative organ (department) shall be required to provide relevant proof; if necessary, the procuratorial organ may conduct its own investigation and verification. If there are doubts about the legality of obtaining the evidence such as witness testimony or victim statements provided by the defendant or his or her defender, the court shall be requested to require them to provide proof.

26. If the defendant or his or her defender raises new evidence or leads after the initiation of public prosecution claiming that evidence is illegal, and the investigative organ (department) cannot provide evidence to prove the legality of the evidence, or the evidence provided is not reliable and sufficient, and other evidence cannot sufficiently prove the defendant's guilt, the prosecution may be withdrawn, and the case may be returned to the investigative organ (department) or a decision not to prosecute may be made.

V. Further Improve the Work Mechanism and Form a Supervisory Synergy

27. Intensify the investigation and handling of illegal and criminal acts such as extortion of confessions by torture and violent evidence collection. The functional departments of investigation supervision, public prosecution, duty crime and infringement prosecution, and prison procuratorial work shall cooperate fully, improve the work mechanism coordinating all aspects such as information sharing, discovery of case leads, transfer of evidence, and case investigation. Further enhance the capacity to discover and handle illegal and criminal acts such as extortion of confessions by torture and violent evidence collection, and effectively curb illegal evidence collection and other illegal acts through timely and effective prosecution of illegal and criminal acts.

28. Improve the linkage mechanism and information resource sharing mechanism between the review of arrest, review of prosecution, and supervision over investigative activities. For cases where arrest is approved or decided but further collection, supplementation, improvement, or fixation of evidence is needed, and for cases where arrest is not approved and supplementary investigation is needed, the investigation supervision department shall propose opinions on supplementing evidence materials, and while sending them to the investigative organ (department), shall send copies to the public prosecution department. The investigation supervision and public prosecution departments shall closely cooperate, track supervision, and urge the investigative organ (department) to supplement and improve evidence. When accepting a case for review and prosecution, it shall be reviewed whether the investigative organ (department) has supplemented the relevant evidence materials in accordance with the supplementary investigation opinions.

29. Further improve and perfect the mechanism for intervening in investigations and guiding evidence collection. The departments of prosecutorial supervision and public prosecution shall strengthen cooperation and mutual constraints with investigative authorities (departments). For cases where intervention in investigations is necessary, as well as cases where the investigative authority (department) requests intervention, they shall promptly intervene, participate in inquests, inspections, re-inspections, and re-examinations, participate in discussions on major cases, and provide suggestions on the collection, fixation, supplementation, and improvement of evidence. Where any illegal circumstances are discovered in investigative activities, they shall promptly issue corrective opinions in accordance with the law.

30. Fully leverage the important role of criminal science and technology in handling cases. The departments responsible for duty crime investigation, prosecutorial supervision, public prosecution, prison and detention supervision, and prosecutorial technology shall work closely together, utilizing technical means to enhance the ability to discover, collect, and fix evidence, and to improve the capability and level of reviewing, judging, and utilizing evidentiary materials involving specialized technical issues.

31. Strengthen communication and coordination with investigative authorities and judicial authorities. Through joint meetings, case quality evaluation and notification, and other means, analyze and study problems discovered in the collection, review, judgment, and utilization of evidence, jointly explore solutions with investigative authorities and judicial authorities, and, in light of local realities, improve and perfect relevant mechanisms and measures for implementing the two "Provisions."

32. Higher people's procuratorates shall continuously summarize experiences and problems in practice, strengthen management, inspection, and supervision, and enhance professional guidance to lower-level people's procuratorates. For major criminal cases, cases that have significant influence nationwide or locally, cases supervised by higher people's procuratorates, and cases where, after coordination by relevant departments, the coordinating opinions are inconsistent with those of the procuratorial authority, the lower-level people's procuratorate shall promptly report to the higher-level people's procuratorate.
